title: ApexBridge - Usage Lab: Route Economics Walkthrough
summary: Intro demo of Redwood Console route-level telemetry and cost decomposition. Focus: how to attribute per-feature spend, set SLOs, and run a short pilot to validate latency and unit economics. Customer has a mixed hosted + on-prem strategy and wants clear cost split for chargeback. ACTIONS: share SOC2 + security pack, send pilot proposal, schedule bench run with sample traffic.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 and compliance pack (link)
Prepare 2-week pilot proposal with dedicated routes and traffic profile
Schedule benchmarks on Tuesday next week (Roberto + Liam)
Janelle to confirm internal stakeholders and billing owner
action_items: Maya Chen - Send pilot proposal and sample pricing spreadsheet - 2026-12-03
Liam Ortega - Prepare benchmark script and sample traffic generator, run with ApexBridge flags - 2026-12-01
Sana Patel - Provide 7-day traffic profile and top 10 routes - 2026-11-30
Janelle Park - Share billing owner contact and current cost buckets - 2026-12-04
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-26 15:00 PST / Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Sana Patel (ApexBridge), Roberto Diaz (ApexBridge), Janelle Park (ApexBridge FinOps)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really quick intro — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Liam, our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Liam: hi! thanks for the time, we'll try to keep it practical — show the console, per-route cost attribution, and then dive into the pilot idea.
[00:20] Sana: thanks, excited. quick context — we run a hybrid setup, some inference in-house for sensitive models, and hosted for lower-sensitivity endpoints. main ask is per-feature cost so finance can do chargeback.
[00:38] Maya: perfect, that maps well. high level we'll show three things: route dashboards, token-level costing, and an ops playbook for scaling.
[00:50] Liam: jumping in, this is the Redwood Console home. note — the telemetry ingestion is via a small agent or cloud webhook, we map requests to routes by path and metadata. sometimes the automatic mapping confuses similar endpoints so we recommend explicit route tags.
[01:20] Roberto: can you show how a route looks when it's multi-model? e.g., our chat flow picks model variants depending on length.
[01:33] Liam: yes, so the route view surfaces model variant splits — you'll see percent of traffic per model, average tokens in/out, p95 latency, and cost per 1k tokens. (small pause) Uh, apologies — there's a slight hiccup on the demo dataset, some user IDs are redacted but that's fine.
[02:05] [screen share] Liam: here's the per-route timeline. notice the 'cost delta' column — that's where we attribute extra spend to things like long-context completions or bad prompt formatting. you can filter by model, region, and quantization profile.
[02:42] Sana: that "cost delta" — how does it handle KV cache hits vs misses? we rely a lot on prefix cache.
[02:55] Liam: good question — we infer KV cache effectiveness from repeated prefix matches; if you have explicit cache telemetry we can ingest it and show cache hit ratios. our math adjusts the per-token billing to reflect cached tokens so you don't double-charge. sometimes the transcripted field shows 'K V cache' in the logs, so we rely on mapping rules.
[03:30] Janelle: on the finance side we need to map costs to internal charge codes — can we export a daily CSV with route IDs and cost buckets?
[03:43] Liam: yes, exports are a first-class feature. you can pull daily files with columns: route_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, compute_ms, cost_usd. we also have a webhook for pushing cost deltas into your billing system.
[04:10] Maya: also note the token pricing is configurable per model variant — so for Dedicated you might have a different unit-rate than Hosted.
[04:25] Roberto: what about burst capacity — we sometimes see big traffic spikes during campaign launches. how does autoscaling affect cost visibility?
[04:40] Liam: autoscaling is surfaced as capacity events. the console will show reserved vs burst capacity and the incremental cost for burst. we also model per-minute vs per-hour granularity. important caveat: on aggressive autoscale you can see temporary p95 latency drops but spend will spike.
[05:05] Sana: security questions — we need to know if logs are PII-scrubbed and how KMS integrates for private deployment.
[05:18] Maya: we will send the SOC2 and compliance pack after this call. for Private/VPC customers we support customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations, and audit logs. Liam can show the audit log mapping briefly.
[05:35] Liam: here's a sample audit trace — event types, requester, route_id. note transcription sometimes mis-labels requesters, so in real logs we're more precise.
[06:05] [10 minute demo jump — Liam navigates to 'Route Cost Explorer']
[06:12] Liam: Route Cost Explorer lets you group by tag, team, or route. here's a sample where we group by product-team tags — you can see finance view with chargeback-ready export.
[06:40] Janelle: can we attach internal cost centers and have nightly allocation jobs?
[06:48] Liam: yes, allocation rules run nightly; you can define weightings per route or use proportional token split.
[07:10] Roberto: curious about model quantization recommendations — sometimes we want to trade quality for cost. does Redwood provide guidance?
[07:22] Maya: Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles based on your workload: if most requests are short, a 4-bit quant might give 30-40% cost savings with negligible quality loss. Optimize can run an eval set against variants.
[07:45] Sana: can Optimize tie into our regression alerts — we need to know if quality drops post-quantization.
[07:54] Liam: yes, you can attach eval prompt sets; we run automatic A/B and surface failure modes. notification hooks can alert SLO owners.
[08:12] [12:00 mark — deep-dive request from Roberto]
[08:18] Roberto: let's talk about latency SLAs per route — we want p95 under 250ms for user facing chat, others can be higher. can Redwood enforce routing by SLA?
[08:30] Liam: we have routing policies that prefer low-latency instances for routes with tight SLOs and fall back to cost-optimized pools when required. you can configure canary and fallback policies — sample policy here prefers 'edge-optimized' for route chat-main.
[09:00] Janelle: what about cost forecasting — we need monthly projections for finance.
[09:07] Maya: Console has a forecast model based on recent usage, expected promotions, and model changes. it's not perfect but gives a 30/60/90 day projection with confidence bands.
[09:30] Sana: on the hybrid note, we need to avoid double-billing when private and hosted both process parts of a request. how do you dedupe?
[09:45] Liam: we use request IDs and a matching algorithm; if the same request flows through both, we attribute primary execution to the location that did generation. you can also set a 'canonical' route for chargeback. occasionally logs show duplicated session IDs which we normalize.
[10:20] [screen share — sample pilot config shown]
[10:25] Liam: pilot idea: two-week sandbox, 3 key routes, dedicated small pool (g4x-equivalent), traffic replay from your last 7 days, and a bench run to measure p95 and token economics.
[10:45] Roberto: can the bench run simulate cache behaviour? our prefix-heavy chat depends on good cache hit rates.
[10:53] Liam: yes, traffic replay can preserve request ordering and prefix frequency so the KV cache hit ratio mirrors production. we'll include an agent to capture cache metrics.
[11:20] Maya: pricing for pilot — we typically offer usage credits + a flat bench fee to cover dedicated capacity. I'll send a sheet after the call.
[11:34] Janelle: finance will need the detailed line items for the bench fee.
[11:40] Maya: understood.
[12:05] [15:00 — Q/A — security deep-dive]
[12:12] Sana: SSO is big for us — we use Okta with SCIM and need RBAC integration for production.
[12:22] Liam: we support SAML 2.0, SCIM provisioning for groups, and role-based access in the console. for audit we keep immutable logs for 365 days by default in Enterprise plans.
[12:45] Sana: retention policy flexibility? some regs need 7 years.
[12:51] Maya: that's an enterprise add-on; we can catalogue options in the compliance pack.
[13:15] [20:00 — product ops questions]
[13:18] Roberto: suppose a route suddenly increases context length — how quickly can we update quantization or model variant routing?
[13:28] Liam: routing rules are config changes — you can rollout a model variant change with canary at 5% then ramp. quantization needs a new model build but Redwood supports blitting between variants; typical wait is a few hours depending on model size.
[13:55] Janelle: billing cadence for dedicated pools? monthly invoice or usage?
[14:00] Maya: Dedicated is usually reserved capacity billed monthly, with overage billed at a higher unit-rate. we can do custom terms.
[14:15] [30:00 — summary and recaps]
[14:18] Maya: recap — we showed route dashboards, cost exports, autoscale/burst visibility, and the pilot outline. open items are security pack, pilot details, and bench scheduling.
[14:40] Sana: we like the approach. next week Roberto and Liam will do the bench. Janelle will confirm billing contact.
[14:52] Maya: perfect — we'll send SOC2, pilot proposal, and a link to the sample traffic replay tool.
[15:05] Roberto: one last question — if pilot shows 20% higher spend than expected, do you provide recommendations to reduce cost?
[15:14] Liam: yes, Optimize will run post-pilot analysis: batching, quant, and model swaps; we'll prioritize low-effort high-impact changes.
[15:30] Maya: thanks everyone; we'll follow up with the packet.

End of transcript.
